# Running LandWeb

LandWeb runs as a `targets` pipeline.
`_targets.R` defines each step of a run (data preparation, simulation, summaries and the study area report) as a target, and `targets::tar_make()` builds every target that is missing or out of date.
Finished targets are kept in the `_targets/` store, so a later run skips any step whose inputs have not changed.
The numbered scripts in the project root (`00-main.R` to `04-post-sim.R`) are from LandWeb v2 and are not used by the pipeline.

1. Launch Rstudio and open the LandWeb Rstudio project (`LandWeb.Rproj`);

:::{.rmdimportant}
Be sure to use R 4.6.1 when running the model!

If using `rig` to manage multiple R versions, use the following to launch Rstudio with the correct version of R:

```bash
cd ~/GitHub/LandWeb
rig rstudio renv.lock
```
:::

2. Install the package versions the project uses by restoring them from its lockfile (`renv.lock`):

```r
options(renv.config.pak.enabled = FALSE)
renv::restore()
```

:::{.rmdnote}
On a machine with no packages installed yet, the restore can stop while installing `SpaDES.core`, with the error "there is no package called 'ggplot2'".
Packages are installed in parallel, and `SpaDES.core` was built before `ggplot2` was ready.
Restart R and run `renv::restore()` again; the second pass completes.
:::

3. Choose the study areas and the number of replicates in `_local.R` (see [Configuring a run]).

4. Start the run with `targets::tar_make()` (see [Running the model]).

## Configuring a run

### Where settings live

- `_local.R` holds the settings you will usually change:
  - `study_areas`: the study areas to run (see [Choosing study areas]);
  - `n_reps`: the number of replicate simulations per study area;
  - `res`: pixel size in metres (240);
  - `sim_end`: simulation length in years (1000);
  - `local_workers`: how many workers run at once when the whole run is on one machine.
    It also sets each simulation's share of the machine's memory, so changing it re-runs the simulations;
  - `paths`: where inputs, outputs and temporary files go.
    `scratchPath` holds temporary raster files while a simulation runs; it must be a writable directory, ideally on a fast local disk, on every machine that runs simulations.
- `_targets.R` holds the module parameters of each stage.
  Change model parameters here.
- `_hosts.R` (optional, not tracked by git) lists the compute nodes for a run spread over several machines (see [Running on several machines]).

`_local.R` is read only on the machine that runs `tar_make()`; the worker processes that run the simulations do not read it.

Changing a setting or a module parameter re-runs the stages that use it and everything downstream of them.
Every stage uses `paths`, so changing it re-runs the whole pipeline; changing `res` re-runs every study-area stage.
A stage also re-runs when its code changes: a new commit to one of its modules, or a new version of a GitHub-installed package that one of its modules uses.

### Scenario

LandWeb v2 (the 2019 runs) increased seed dispersal distances (`dispersalType = "high"`) to ensure sufficient regeneration following fire, and used `ROStype = "log"`.
These adjustments made the model behave more like a state-transition model than a process-based one.
LandWeb v3 uses the default for both (`dispersalType = "default"` and `ROStype = "default"`, set in `_targets.R`), so it behaves like the standard LANDIS-II model.

### Choosing study areas

LandWeb v3 is run on 18 study areas.
Each is a group of forest tenures (FMAs, TSAs and FMLs) assigned to one ecoregion, and is named after that ecoregion, *e.g.* `WesternAlbertaUpland`.
Report 00 (`reports/pdf/00-overview.pdf`) maps the groups and lists the tenures in each.

To choose which study areas to run, list them in `study_areas` in `_local.R`, *e.g.*:

```r
study_areas = c("WesternAlbertaUpland", "ClearHillsUpland"),
```

Each study area gets its own copy of every study-area stage, named with the study area as a suffix:

- `preamble_<studyArea>`: study area boundaries, land cover, stand age and fire return intervals (`LandWeb_preamble`);
- `speciesData_<studyArea>`: species cover (`Biomass_speciesData`);
- `dataPrep_<studyArea>`: initial cohorts and species-ecoregion parameters (`Biomass_borealDataPrep`);
- `mainSim_<studyArea>`: the simulations, one branch per replicate (`Biomass_core`, `LandMine`, `Biomass_regeneration`, `burnSummaries`, `NRV_summary`);
- `summaries_nrv_<studyArea>` and `summaries_burn_<studyArea>`: summaries across replicates (see [Post-processing analyses]);
- `report05_<studyArea>`: the study area report.

Replicate *n* of a study area always uses random seed *n*.

Two stages are shared by all study areas and built only once:

- `factorial`: a table of simulated growth for combinations of species traits (`Biomass_speciesFactorial`);
- `growthCurves`: the growth-curve fit for every species, from forest plot data (`Biomass_speciesParameters`).

Adding a study area does not rebuild them.

## Running the model

**NOTE:** The first time the model is run, it will automatically download additional data and may install additional R packages, which can take some time to complete.

:::{.rmdcaution}
Due to a server configuration problem, the following national ecolocation polygons should be downloaded manually to the `inputs/` directory:

- **ecodistricts**: [ecodistrict_shp.zip](http://sis.agr.gc.ca/cansis/nsdb/ecostrat/district/ecodistrict_shp.zip)
- **ecoregions**: [ecoregion_shp.zip](http://sis.agr.gc.ca/cansis/nsdb/ecostrat/region/ecoregion_shp.zip)
- **ecozones**: [ecozone_shp.zip](http://sis.agr.gc.ca/cansis/nsdb/ecostrat/zone/ecozone_shp.zip)
:::

:::{.rmdimportant}
Pipeline runs download from Google Drive as the LandWeb service account.
Set up its key file on every machine that runs the pipeline before the first run (see [Data requirements]).
:::

### Starting a run

From an R session in the project directory, check what a run would build:

```r
targets::tar_outdated()   ## targets that would be built
targets::tar_visnetwork() ## the pipeline as a graph
```

Then start the run:

```r
targets::tar_make()
```

or, from a terminal:

```bash
cd ~/GitHub/LandWeb
Rscript-4.6.1 -e 'targets::tar_make()'
```

`tar_make()` builds the targets in order of their dependencies, and runs independent targets, such as different study areas and replicates, at the same time in separate worker processes.
Only one `tar_make()` can run on a store at a time.

:::{.rmdimportant}
A full run takes days: one replicate of a large study area can take most of a day.
On Linux, start it as a `systemd` user unit, so that it keeps running after you log out or close Rstudio:

```bash
cd ~/GitHub/LandWeb
mkdir -p logs
systemd-run --user --collect --unit=landweb-run --working-directory="$PWD" \
  bash -c "Rscript-4.6.1 -e 'targets::tar_make()' > logs/landweb-run.log 2>&1"
```

Follow it with `tail -f logs/landweb-run.log`, or with `targets::tar_progress()` from an R session.
Stop it with `systemctl --user stop landweb-run`.
The unit keeps running after you log out only if lingering is enabled for your account (`loginctl enable-linger`).
:::

### Outputs and logs

Each study area's results are under `outputs/<studyArea>/`.
Results shared by all study areas are in directories at the `outputs/` root whose names start with an underscore.

```
outputs/
  <studyArea>/
    preamble/  speciesData/  dataPrep/  data preparation, each with figures/
    mainSim/
      rep01/ ... repNN/     one directory per replicate, with figures/
      figures/              figures across replicates
      *.csv, *.tif          fire summaries across replicates, and the
                            species tables the simulations used
    postprocess/            NRV summaries: tables (csv/) and figures/
    reports/                the study area report, 05-<studyArea>.pdf
    logs/                   one log per stage and replicate
  _factorial/               shared species trait table (built once)
  _growthCurves/            shared growth-curve fit (built once)
logs/                       run logs; worker logs in logs/crew/
```

- `outputs/<studyArea>/logs/` holds the log of each stage (`preamble.log`, `dataPrep.log`, `mainSim_rep01.log`, ...), with its warnings in a matching `*_warnings.txt` file.
- `logs/crew/` holds the logs of the worker processes.
- The output of `tar_make()` itself goes wherever you send it; the example above writes it to `logs/landweb-run.log`.

The study area report is also copied into `reports/pdf/`.

To find out why a target failed, `targets::tar_meta(fields = error, complete_only = TRUE)` lists the failed targets with their error messages; the stage's log has the details.

### Rebuilding part of a run

`targets::tar_make(names = ...)` builds the named targets, together with any outdated targets they depend on.
Because a stage re-runs whenever its modules, or the GitHub-installed packages they use, change, an existing store can show most stages as outdated after a package update, even though their stored results are still the ones you want.
A plain `tar_make()` or `tar_make(names = ...)` would then re-run the whole chain, which takes days.
To rebuild only the named targets, from the stored results of the targets upstream of them, add `shortcut = TRUE`:

```r
targets::tar_make(names = mainSim_WesternAlbertaUpland, shortcut = TRUE)
targets::tar_make(names = mainSim_WesternAlbertaUpland_files, shortcut = TRUE)
targets::tar_make(
  names = c(summaries_nrv_WesternAlbertaUpland, summaries_burn_WesternAlbertaUpland),
  shortcut = TRUE
)
```

Each module stage (`preamble`, `speciesData`, `dataPrep`, `mainSim` and the summaries) has a companion target, `<stage>_<studyArea>_files`, that records the files the stage wrote, and the stages downstream depend on it.
The shared stages have one too (`factorial_files`, `growthCurves_files`).
After rebuilding a stage with `shortcut = TRUE`, rebuild its `_files` target as well, as above.
Otherwise the downstream stages still see the old files, and are skipped as up to date.

The check for code changes reads the packages installed on the machine that loads `_targets.R`.
Run `tar_outdated()` and `tar_make()` only where the project library matches `renv.lock` (run `renv::restore()` first); elsewhere the whole store looks outdated.

## Post-processing analyses

The pipeline summarizes each study area's replicates once all of them have finished; there is no separate post-processing step.
`n_reps` in `_local.R` sets how many replicates the summaries combine.

- `summaries_nrv_<studyArea>` (`NRV_summary`) builds the natural range of variation of landscape and patch metrics, leading vegetation cover, and large patches, for each set of reporting polygons within the study area.
  Its outputs, including boxplots and histograms of leading vegetation cover and histograms of large patches, are in `outputs/<studyArea>/postprocess/`.
- `summaries_burn_<studyArea>` (`burnSummaries`) builds the fire-size distribution and the mean annual burn maps, simulated and historic, across replicates, in `outputs/<studyArea>/mainSim/`.
- `report05_<studyArea>` renders the study area report from these summaries.

## Advanced setup

### Running on several machines

The pipeline can send its heavy stages to other machines (compute nodes) over SSH, using the `crew.ssh` package.
On the machine that runs `tar_make()` (the control node), copy `_hosts.R.example` to `_hosts.R` and edit it: list the compute nodes and how many workers each can run (`crew.ssh.nodes`), the project path (`crew.ssh.projdir`), and the shared directories to link into the project on each node (`crew.ssh.symlinks`).
`_hosts.R` holds machine names, so it is not tracked by git.
Without it, `tar_make()` runs up to `local_workers` workers on its own machine.

This needs:

- SSH access without a password prompt from the control node to each compute node;
- the project cloned at the same path on every machine;
- `_targets/`, `inputs/` and `outputs/` on storage that every machine shares.

Before each run, bring every compute node up to date with the control node:

```bash
cd ~/GitHub/LandWeb
Rscript-4.6.1 scripts/sync-nodes.R --dry-run  ## show what it would do
Rscript-4.6.1 scripts/sync-nodes.R
```

On each node, `sync-nodes.R` fast-forwards the project's git branch from GitHub, updates the submodules, re-creates the shared-directory links, and runs `renv::restore()`.
Nodes pull from GitHub and restore the committed `renv.lock`, so commit and push your changes first.
Do not sync while a run is in progress: it would change the packages under the running workers.

### Caching

The pipeline turns off SpaDES caching (`reproducible.useCache = FALSE`, and `.useCache = FALSE` for each module); the `_targets/` store decides what re-runs.

### Speeding up disk-based operations

Disk-based file operations benefit from using a solid state drive (SSD) instead of a conventional spinning hard drive.
Point `scratchPath` in `_local.R` at an SSD on each machine that runs simulations.
`inputs/`, `outputs/` and `_targets/` can be symbolic links to other storage, *e.g.* a larger shared drive.
